contracts.title: One write can never make the vault unopenable
contracts.closes: Closes G91: writing notes/a.md and then notes/a.md/b.md is accepted by checkPath, the second put is appended to the op log and fdatasynced (src/engine/vault.mjs:226) before mkdirSync throws EEXIST (:235), and every later Vault.open() throws EEXIST from recover() (:119, called unguarded at :66), even after the file is deleted by hand, because recover() first rebuilds it. The daemon, the doctor, compact and the runner can never open the vault again. Any token with write scope over a matching path reaches it (MCP memev_write and memev_append, HTTP PUT and PATCH, the tunnel when remote access is on): a remote denial of service on the vault. Found by the SR-1.22 red-team round and reproduced on 31 October 2026 at main be457db
contracts.status: proposed: owner's go pending, signs after a clean red-team round

contracts.title: Done comes only from a passing verify
contracts.closes: Closes G92 (issue #242) and the PROTECTED part of issue #243: contractList sets a signed contract's state to done whenever a file named contracts/closed/<id>.json exists (src/engine/contracts.mjs:262-265), and nothing checks what the file holds or who wrote it. PROTECTED covers only contracts/signed/ and contracts/keys/ (src/engine/vault.mjs:27), verify writes contracts/closed/ through the caller's own identity (contracts.mjs:248), and contracts/receipts/ is unprotected. So any token with write scope over contracts/**, including the token a paired device gets (src/engine/devices.mjs:85) and a cloud connector's (src/server/oauth.mjs:17), takes a contract out of the Stop-hook gate and the pre-push gate with no contract.verified record, and can rewrite its receipts. Found by the SR-0.03 red-team round and reproduced on 31 October 2026 on the main source
contracts.status: proposed: owner's go pending, signs after a clean red-team round

contracts.title: The bus writes its own routing files
contracts.closes: Closes G93 (issue #250): connector and device tokens hold write on bus/** (src/engine/devices.mjs:85, src/server/oauth.mjs:17), and the bus's routing files are plain vault notes: bus/operator.json names the operator and bus/seats/<seat>.json carries renamed_from. So a note write makes a cloud connector the operator, its task to the 'operator' alias carries operator authority, and a runner turned on for a local seat starts its command headless with the connector's text as the prompt. Found by the SR-1.25 red-team round and reproduced on 31 October 2026 on the main source
contracts.status: proposed: owner's go pending, signs after a clean red-team round

contracts.title: A hook starts without loading the whole CLI
contracts.closes: Closes G94: the MEM-098 latency test (test/hooks-latency.test.mjs:64: the prompt hook returns in under 1.5 s while each backend call takes 1 s) fails on the CI runner at 1589 to 1729 ms on 32 of 37 open pull requests, after passing on 28 to 30 October. The hook runs through bin/memev.mjs, which loads the whole CLI (src/cli/main.mjs) for every hook, and src/cli/hooks.mjs loads the engine at start through isVault (src/engine/vault.mjs) and the transcript scanner. Measured on 31 October 2026 on a development machine: node starts in 40 ms, importing main.mjs takes 110 ms and hooks.mjs 140 ms, and the test passes there at 1322 ms. Every hook event calls isVault, which lives in the engine module (src/engine/vault.mjs:39). The fix is to the hook's own start-up, never to the budget
contracts.status: proposed: owner's go pending, signs after a clean red-team round

contracts.title: Bus messages reach the model as untrusted data, and the open routes are stated
contracts.closes: Closes G98: the seed-stage analysis of 30 October 2026 (D12, D10). The hook text quotes the body of a bus message from any seat but the operator as untrusted data and cuts it to 200 characters (src/server/http.mjs:98, UNTRUSTED_BODY at :36), but the MCP bus tools bus_unread, bus_since and bus_tail hand the model each message with its raw body (src/server/mcp.mjs:167-174, through vault.bus.unread, since and tail), and docs/THREAT-MODEL.md:15 says so; the last message bus_roster shows per seat is the same. GET /healthz and the invite redeem route answer without a token by design; /healthz gives the vault id to a direct local caller and {ok:true} to any other (http.mjs:123), and the threat model has no row saying why the two routes are open and what each discloses
